policy: Official full-text links only; read source terms before copying.

groups.title: Foundations & Logic
groups.description: Proofs, logic, set theory, computability and model theory

groups.title: Algebra
groups.description: Linear, abstract, commutative and homological algebra; categories, representations and algebraic geometry

groups.title: Analysis
groups.description: Calculus, real and complex analysis, measure, functional analysis, Fourier analysis and differential equations

groups.title: Geometry & Topology
groups.description: Point-set and algebraic topology, differential geometry, homotopy and symplectic geometry

groups.title: Number Theory
groups.description: Elementary, algebraic and analytic number theory; class field theory, modular forms and arithmetic geometry

groups.title: Discrete Mathematics
groups.description: Combinatorics, graphs, enumeration and generating functions

groups.title: Probability & Dynamics
groups.description: Undergraduate and measure-theoretic probability, dynamical systems and ergodic theory

books.title: Book of Proof
books.author: Richard Hammack
books.note: A transition from calculation to proofs, with sets, induction and cardinality. Selected solutions help self-study; it is preparation rather than an advanced subject text.

books.title: forall x: Calgary
books.author: P. D. Magnus, Tim Button, Aaron Thomas-Bolduc and Richard Zach, with contributors
books.note: Introduces formal languages, truth tables and natural deduction. Exercises and solutions support a first logic course; metatheory is developed further in the next text.
books.label: Full HTML & PDF

books.title: Sets, Logic, Computation
books.author: Richard Zach
books.note: Develops completeness, compactness and undecidability after elementary formal logic. A structured bridge from proof systems to mathematical metatheory.
books.label: Full book & PDF

books.title: Incompleteness and Computability
books.author: Richard Zach
books.note: Covers recursive functions, arithmetization and Gödel's theorems. Best read after a first metalogic course, not as an introduction to proofs.
books.label: Full book & PDF

books.title: Open Logic Text
books.author: The Open Logic Project
books.version: Rolling complete build; distinct from the legacy Calgary textbooks
books.note: A modular collection spanning logic, computability, set theory and model theory. Chapters can be selected for a course.

books.title: Set Theory: An Open Introduction
books.author: Tim Button
books.note: Explains the set-theoretic foundations of mathematics and the motivation for ZFC. Its emphasis is conceptual and philosophical, not graduate forcing theory.
books.label: Full book & PDF

books.title: Lecture Notes — Model Theory (Math 411)
books.author: Anand Pillay
books.note: A concise graduate treatment beginning with structures and languages. The lecture-note format rewards familiarity with logical notation and independent proof work.

books.title: Linear Algebra
books.author: Jim Hefferon
books.note: Balances Gaussian elimination with vector spaces and proofs. Worked solutions to all exercises are useful for independent study; suitable before an operator-focused second course.
books.label: Full book & solutions

books.title: Linear Algebra Done Right, 4th edition
books.author: Sheldon Axler
books.note: A proof-based, operator-centered second course that introduces determinants late. Especially useful for structural understanding; not designed primarily as a computational matrix handbook.

books.title: Abstract Algebra: Theory and Applications
books.author: Thomas W. Judson
books.note: Groups, rings and fields are accompanied by applications and exercises. Reviewers note broad undergraduate coverage; a useful first algebra text rather than a graduate reference.
books.label: Read full HTML

books.title: Group Theory
books.author: J. S. Milne
books.note: A compact graduate introduction, including finite-group representations. Concise exposition makes prior exposure to algebra helpful.

books.title: Fields and Galois Theory
books.author: J. S. Milne
books.note: Develops field extensions, Galois theory and transcendence degree. A focused continuation after groups, rings and basic fields.

books.title: A Primer of Commutative Algebra
books.author: J. S. Milne
books.note: A concise foundation for algebraic geometry and number theory, covering localization, integrality, dimension and completion. 'Introductory' here presupposes substantial algebra.

books.title: A Term of Commutative Algebra
books.author: Allen Altman and Steven Kleiman
books.note: A course-sized development with exercises and solutions. Suitable for systematic study after abstract algebra; its ring-and-module language is more demanding than a first algebra course.
books.label: Full PDF via MIT

books.title: Notes on Basic Homological Algebra
books.author: Andrew Baker
books.note: A compact entry into homological methods for readers already comfortable with modules. Useful as course notes; less expansive than a comprehensive graduate textbook.

books.title: The Stacks Project — Homological Algebra
books.author: The Stacks Project Authors
books.note: A detailed searchable reference with stable theorem tags. Use the Homology, Derived Categories and related chapters; it is not a gentle sequential first course.
books.label: Read full reference

books.title: Lectures on Cyclic Homology
books.author: Dale Husemoller
books.version: TIFR volume 83; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Develops cyclic and Hochschild homology. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Category Theory in Context
books.author: Emily Riehl
books.note: Explains universal properties, Yoneda, adjunctions and Kan extensions through mathematical examples. Algebra and topology greatly improve accessibility despite minimal formal prerequisites.

books.title: Elements of ∞-Category Theory
books.author: Emily Riehl and Dominic Verity
books.note: A substantial treatment of higher categories for mathematically mature readers. A later step after ordinary category theory, not a shortcut around its foundations.

books.title: Introduction to Representation Theory
books.author: Pavel Etingof et al.
books.note: Introduces representations using algebra and many exercises. Appropriate for strong undergraduates with linear algebra; the pace assumes comfort with abstract structures.
books.prerequisites: Linear algebra; groups, rings and fields.

books.title: Lie Groups and Lie Algebras I
books.author: Pavel Etingof
books.note: A graduate course connecting Lie groups, Lie algebras and representations. Initial manifold material helps orientation but does not remove the need for mathematical maturity.
books.prerequisites: Abstract algebra; topology and smooth manifolds.

books.title: Tensor Categories
books.author: Pavel Etingof, Shlomo Gelaki, Dmitri Nikshych and Victor Ostrik
books.note: Develops the categorical setting for representation theory. A specialist continuation rather than an introductory algebra text; link to the authorized author-hosted edition.
books.label: Full book via author's page

books.title: Algebraic Geometry
books.author: J. S. Milne
books.note: A first graduate course centered on abstract algebraic varieties, providing a bridge toward schemes.
books.prerequisites: Fields, Galois theory and commutative algebra.

books.title: The Rising Sea: Foundations of Algebraic Geometry
books.author: Ravi Vakil
books.note: A broad, exercise-rich development of schemes and their geometry. The October 21, 2025 author edition closely matches the published text; substantial algebra is essential.
books.archiveNote: July 27, 2024 archive · CC BY-NC-ND 3.0; unchanged noncommercial copy.

books.title: The Stacks Project
books.author: The Stacks Project Authors
books.note: An extensive open reference on schemes and related algebra. Stable tags are useful for precise citations; selective consultation is more practical than cover-to-cover reading.
books.label: Read full reference

books.title: Stacks and Moduli
books.author: Jarod Alper
books.version: January 5, 2026 draft
books.note: A systematic development of algebraic stacks and moduli, with substantial geometric examples. The linked version is an author draft, not a claim of a final published edition.
books.use: Study stacks after a first graduate algebraic geometry course.

books.title: Lectures on Étale Cohomology
books.author: J. S. Milne
books.version: v2.21, March 2013
books.note: Develops étale morphisms, sites and cohomology through base change and the Weil conjectures. These freely available course notes are not the separate 1980 Princeton book.
books.use: First sustained study of étale cohomology.

books.title: Spectral Algebraic Geometry
books.author: Jacob Lurie
books.version: February 2018; author labels it under construction
books.note: A research reference for spectral schemes, stacks and their sheaves. The author explicitly warns that the draft is unfinished and contains broken references.
books.prerequisites: Higher Topos Theory; Higher Algebra; schemes.
books.use: Selective reference, not a first introduction.

books.title: Homotopical Algebraic Geometry I: Topos Theory
books.author: Bertrand Toën and Gabriele Vezzosi
books.version: 2002 / published 2005; latest version on arXiv
books.note: Constructs homotopical sites, stacks and topoi using model categories.
books.use: Compare model-categorical foundations with infinity-categorical ones.

books.title: Homotopical Algebraic Geometry II: Geometric Stacks and Applications
books.author: Bertrand Toën and Gabriele Vezzosi
books.version: 2004; revised 2006; latest version on arXiv
books.note: Develops geometric derived stacks and applications to moduli. Distinct from the foundational first volume.
books.use: Research preparation in derived moduli problems.

books.title: Derived Algebraic Geometry
books.author: Bertrand Toën
books.version: 2014; latest version on arXiv
books.note: An overview of derived geometry, deformation theory and its connections with quantization.
books.use: Orient a reading programme before technical monographs.

books.title: Algebraic Geometry over C∞-Rings
books.author: Dominic Joyce
books.version: 2009; revised 2016; latest version on arXiv
books.note: Develops the algebraic language underlying smooth and derived differential geometry.
books.use: Bridge algebraic geometry and smooth geometric constructions.

books.title: D-Manifolds and D-Orbifolds: A Theory of Derived Differential Geometry
books.author: Dominic Joyce
books.version: 2012 preliminary version, 768 pages
books.note: The complete available preliminary manuscript develops virtual smooth geometry. The author warns that later published definitions differ; it is not the final OUP book.
books.use: Detailed study of derived smooth objects.

books.title: Derived Smooth Manifolds
books.author: David I. Spivak
books.version: 2008 / Duke 2010; latest version on arXiv
books.note: Constructs derived manifolds using homotopical sheaf-theoretic methods.
books.use: Compare another foundation for derived differential geometry.

books.title: Triangulated Categories of Mixed Motives
books.author: Denis-Charles Cisinski and Frédéric Déglise
books.version: 2019 arXiv version; latest version on arXiv
books.note: Builds motivic categories and the six-operation formalism in a systematic treatment.
books.prerequisites: Schemes; triangulated categories; motivic homotopy theory.
books.use: Long-term reference for motives and functoriality.

books.title: Grothendieck’s Six Operations and Vanishing Cycles in the Motivic World, I–II
books.author: Joseph Ayoub
books.version: Astérisque 314–315, 2007; two volumes counted once
books.note: A foundational French treatment of motivic operations and nearby-cycle constructions. The archive supplies the full first volume; the companion volume is Astérisque 315.
books.prerequisites: Motivic homotopy theory; triangulated categories; schemes.
books.use: Research reference for the six-functor formalism.
books.originalTitle: Les six opérations de Grothendieck et le formalisme des cycles évanescents dans le monde motivique (I–II)
books.label: Open archive & full PDF

books.title: Six Lectures on Motives
books.author: Marc Levine
books.version: ICTP lecture manuscript; 61 pages
books.note: Introduces pure motives, mixed-motive constructions and motivic cohomology in a compact course.
books.use: Bridge from cycles to advanced motivic references.

books.title: Perfectoid Spaces
books.author: Peter Scholze
books.version: 2011 / published 2012; latest version on arXiv
books.note: Introduces perfectoid spaces and tilting. This is the foundational paper, not an elementary textbook.
books.prerequisites: Rigid geometry; valuation theory; étale cohomology.
books.use: Read after a course in p-adic geometry.

books.title: Étale Cohomology of Diamonds
books.author: Peter Scholze
books.version: Author manuscript; consult title page for revisions
books.note: Develops diamonds and their étale sheaves, including functorial cohomological machinery.
books.prerequisites: Perfectoid spaces; étale cohomology; derived categories.

books.title: Prisms and Prismatic Cohomology
books.author: Bhargav Bhatt and Peter Scholze
books.version: 2019 / Annals 2022; latest version on arXiv
books.note: Introduces prisms and a cohomology theory connecting several integral p-adic theories.
books.prerequisites: Commutative algebra; p-adic Hodge theory; derived methods.
books.use: Foundational research reading, not a first textbook.

books.title: Integral p-adic Hodge Theory
books.author: Bhargav Bhatt, Matthew Morrow and Peter Scholze
books.version: Published 2018; author version
books.note: Develops integral comparison constructions using perfectoid methods.
books.prerequisites: Perfectoid spaces; étale cohomology; derived algebra.

books.title: Topological Hochschild Homology and Integral p-adic Hodge Theory
books.author: Bhargav Bhatt, Matthew Morrow and Peter Scholze
books.version: Published 2019; author version
books.note: Connects topological Hochschild and cyclic homology to integral p-adic comparison theory.
books.prerequisites: BMS integral theory; spectra; THH and TC.
books.use: Connect arithmetic geometry with stable homotopy theory.

books.title: p-adic Hodge Theory
books.author: Bhargav Bhatt
books.version: Fall 2025 course notes
books.note: A recent course approaching p-adic comparison theory and its geometric foundations.
books.use: A guided route toward contemporary arithmetic geometry.

books.title: Absolute Prismatic Cohomology
books.author: Bhargav Bhatt and Jacob Lurie
books.version: 2022; latest version on arXiv
books.note: Studies absolute prismatic crystals through the Cartier–Witt stack.

books.title: The Prismatization of p-adic Formal Schemes
books.author: Bhargav Bhatt and Jacob Lurie
books.version: 2022; latest version on arXiv
books.note: Provides a stack-theoretic interpretation of prismatic crystals and cohomology.

books.title: Six-Functor Formalisms
books.author: Peter Scholze
books.version: WS 2022–23; updated October 2025
books.note: Studies abstract structures governing operations on sheaf-like categories.
books.prerequisites: Higher categories; sheaf theory; derived categories.
books.use: Organize functorial tools used across modern geometry.

books.title: Berkeley Lectures on p-adic Geometry
books.author: Peter Scholze and Jared Weinstein
books.version: 2020 author-hosted edition
books.note: A sustained course on perfectoid spaces and p-adic geometry with arithmetic applications.
books.use: Prepare for diamonds and modern p-adic research.

books.title: The pro-étale Topology for Schemes
books.author: Bhargav Bhatt and Peter Scholze
books.version: Astérisque 369, 2015
books.note: Develops a topology suited to stronger sheaf-theoretic constructions on schemes.

books.title: Geometrization of the Local Langlands Correspondence
books.author: Laurent Fargues and Peter Scholze
books.version: Author manuscript; consult source for revision
books.note: A research-scale synthesis of the Fargues–Fontaine curve, moduli and local Langlands.

books.title: Condensed Mathematics and Complex Geometry
books.author: Peter Scholze
books.version: Summer semester 2022
books.note: Develops analytic ideas through condensed methods with applications in complex geometry.
books.prerequisites: Condensed mathematics; analytic geometry; higher algebra.
books.use: Study the interface between analysis and modern geometry.

books.title: Lectures on an Introduction to Grothendieck’s Theory of the Fundamental Group
books.author: J. P. Murre
books.version: TIFR volume 40; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Develops the algebraic fundamental group via finite étale covers. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on Deformations of Singularities
books.author: Michael Artin
books.version: TIFR volume 54; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Studies deformation problems and algebraic singularities. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.
books.use: Background for moduli and deformation theory.

books.title: Lectures on Minimal Models and Birational Transformations of Two-Dimensional Schemes
books.author: I. R. Shafarevich
books.version: TIFR volume 37; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Develops classical birational geometry of surfaces. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.
books.use: Compare classical surfaces with modern birational methods.

books.title: Lectures on Moduli of Curves
books.author: David Gieseker
books.version: TIFR volume 69; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: A course devoted to constructions in the moduli theory of curves. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on Frobenius Splittings and B-Modules
books.author: Wilberd van der Kallen
books.version: TIFR volume 84; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Studies positive-characteristic geometric and representation-theoretic methods. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.
books.use: Connect Frobenius techniques and representation theory.

books.title: Calculus, Volume 1
books.author: Gilbert Strang and Edwin 'Jed' Herman
books.note: An illustrated first course with examples and applications. Useful for computational foundations; a proof-based real analysis text is needed for a mathematics-major transition.

books.title: Basic Analysis I
books.author: Jiří Lebl
books.note: Builds real-line analysis before metric spaces, with many exercises. Reviewers describe it as adaptable to undergraduate courses; self-study requires actively writing proofs.

books.title: Basic Analysis II
books.author: Jiří Lebl
books.note: Continues to multivariable analysis, inverse and implicit function theorems, approximation and Fourier series. A natural sequel, not a replacement for measure theory.

books.title: Lectures on Approximation by Polynomials
books.author: J. C. Burkill
books.version: TIFR volume 16; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Treats classical polynomial approximation. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on Potential Theory
books.author: Marcel Brelot
books.version: TIFR volume 19; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Treats classical harmonic and potential-theoretic constructions. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.
books.use: Prepare for potential-theoretic approaches to PDE.

books.title: Lectures on Topics in Analysis
books.author: Raghavan Narasimhan
books.version: TIFR volume 34; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: A selection of advanced analytic topics. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Measure, Integration & Real Analysis
books.author: Sheldon Axler
books.note: A graduate treatment of measure and integration with connections to functional analysis and Fourier analysis. Suitable after proof-based analysis, not elementary calculus.

books.title: An Introduction to Measure Theory
books.author: Terence Tao
books.version: 2011; author online-text link and errata
books.note: Develops Lebesgue measure, integration and related convergence theorems. Follow the author’s online-text link for the full manuscript.
books.use: Bridge undergraduate analysis and graduate integration.
books.label: Author page & full-text link

books.title: Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis: Working the Complex Field
books.author: Jiří Lebl
books.note: A first graduate course from holomorphic functions to conformal mapping and analytic continuation. Appendices review analysis prerequisites; exercises remain important for understanding.
books.prerequisites: Real analysis; metric spaces; multivariable calculus.

books.title: Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables
books.author: Jiří Lebl
books.note: A course-length tour of pseudoconvexity, CR geometry and the ∂̄-problem. Broad exposure rather than an exhaustive reference, with exercises used throughout.

books.title: Lectures on the Theory of Functions of Several Complex Variables
books.author: Bernard Malgrange
books.version: TIFR volume 13; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Develops analytic methods in several complex variables. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on Meromorphic Functions
books.author: W. K. Hayman
books.version: TIFR volume 17; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Develops value-distribution techniques for meromorphic functions. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on Levi Convexity of Complex Manifolds and Cohomology Vanishing Theorems
books.author: Edoardo Vesentini
books.version: TIFR volume 39; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Relates complex geometry and analytic vanishing methods. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.
books.use: Study analytic tools in complex geometry.

books.title: Introduction to Functional Analysis (18.102)
books.author: Richard Melrose
books.note: A course-length development of Banach spaces, Lebesgue integration, Hilbert spaces and applications. The author notes ongoing revisions; useful before more specialized graduate functional analysis.
books.prerequisites: Proof-based real analysis; metric spaces; linear algebra.

books.title: Lectures on Semi-Group Theory and its Application to Cauchy’s Problem in Partial Differential Equations
books.author: Kôsaku Yosida
books.version: TIFR volume 8; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Develops operator semigroups for evolution equations. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on Some Fixed Point Theorems of Functional Analysis
books.author: F. F. Bonsall
books.version: TIFR volume 26; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Develops fixed-point principles in functional-analytic settings. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on the Ekeland Variational Principle with Applications and Detours
books.author: Djairo G. de Figueiredo
books.version: TIFR volume 81; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Develops variational techniques for existence and optimization. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.
books.use: Apply variational principles to nonlinear problems.

books.title: The Fourier Transform and its Applications
books.author: Brad Osgood
books.note: An example-driven introduction from Stanford's EE261 course. Useful for Fourier intuition and applications; follow with a measure-theoretic treatment for deeper analysis.
books.prerequisites: Calculus, complex numbers and linear algebra.

books.title: Lectures on Mean Periodic Functions
books.author: Jean-Pierre Kahane
books.version: TIFR volume 15; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Studies translation and approximation structures in harmonic analysis. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on Topics in Mean Periodic Functions and the Two-Radius Theorem
books.author: Jean Delsarte
books.version: TIFR volume 22; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: A focused treatment of mean-periodic phenomena and uniqueness. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Notes on Diffy Qs: Differential Equations for Engineers
books.author: Jiří Lebl
books.note: Introduces ODEs with computation, modeling and examples. A useful first encounter, but its engineering orientation should be supplemented by proof-based analysis.

books.title: Distributions, Elliptic Regularity, and Applications to PDEs
books.author: Semyon Dyatlov
books.note: Develops distributions and elliptic methods through applications including Hodge theory. These graduate notes are a specialized analytic path, not an elementary PDE survey.
books.prerequisites: Real and functional analysis; Fourier analysis.

books.title: Lectures on Elliptic Partial Differential Equations
books.author: Jacques-Louis Lions
books.version: TIFR volume 10; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Introduces elliptic boundary-value problems and variational methods. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on Mixed Problems in Partial Differential Equations and Representations of Semi-Groups
books.author: Laurent Schwartz
books.version: TIFR volume 11; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Studies mixed PDE problems through operator methods. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on Cauchy Problem
books.author: Sigeru Mizohata
books.version: TIFR volume 35; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Studies initial-value problems for partial differential equations. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on Wave Propagation
books.author: G. B. Whitham
books.version: TIFR volume 61; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Develops mathematical methods for propagating waves. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on Diffusion Problems and Partial Differential Equations
books.author: S. R. S. Varadhan
books.version: TIFR volume 64; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Connects diffusion processes with analytical PDE methods. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on Nonlinear Waves and Shocks
books.author: Cathleen S. Morawetz
books.version: TIFR volume 67; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Studies nonlinear wave phenomena and shock formation. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.

books.title: Lectures on Partial Differential Equations
books.author: Gerald B. Folland
books.version: TIFR volume 70; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Introduces Fourier-analytic techniques for PDE. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.
books.use: Focused graduate course in analytical methods.

books.title: An Introduction to Mathematical Optimal Control Theory
books.author: Lawrence C. Evans
books.version: Author course manuscript
books.note: Develops deterministic and stochastic control ideas alongside differential equations and variational methods.
books.prerequisites: ODE; real analysis; probability for later sections.

books.title: Topology Without Tears
books.author: Sidney A. Morris
books.note: A first course emphasizing topological definitions and proof practice. Useful before algebraic topology; elementary prerequisites do not mean the abstractions require little effort.

books.title: Algebraic Topology
books.author: Allen Hatcher
books.note: Geometric examples accompany fundamental groups, homology and cohomology. A substantial first graduate text; 'introductory' refers to the field, not to university mathematics.
books.archiveNote: 2000 archive · noncommercial paper or electronic copies permitted; other rights reserved.

books.title: Categorical Homotopy Theory
books.author: Emily Riehl
books.note: Develops homotopy-theoretic constructions in a categorical setting. A continuation after basic topology and category theory rather than a first topology course.

books.title: Higher Topos Theory
books.author: Jacob Lurie
books.version: April 2017 author version; book 2009
books.note: Develops infinity-categories, limits, sheaves and infinity-topoi.
books.prerequisites: Category theory; simplicial sets; homotopy theory.
books.use: Foundational reference for higher category theory.

books.title: Higher Algebra
books.author: Jacob Lurie
books.version: September 2017 author version
books.note: Develops stable infinity-categories, operads and algebra objects.
books.use: Reference for modern derived and spectral algebra.

books.title: Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra
books.author: Denis-Charles Cisinski
books.version: 2019 author edition
books.note: A systematic route from homotopical algebra to higher categories.
books.prerequisites: Category theory; simplicial sets; algebraic topology.
books.use: An alternative foundational route to infinity-categories.

books.title: Kerodon
books.author: Jacob Lurie
books.version: Continuously revised online text; checked October 11, 2026
books.note: An online reference for categorical and homotopical foundations, organized by stable tags.

books.title: A Concise Course in Algebraic Topology
books.author: J. Peter May
books.version: Revised author PDF, 2007; book 1999
books.note: A compact treatment of fundamental algebraic-topological constructions.

books.title: The Geometry of Iterated Loop Spaces
books.author: J. Peter May
books.version: Lecture Notes in Mathematics 271, 1972
books.note: Develops operadic approaches to iterated loop spaces.
books.use: Study classical foundations of operads in topology.

books.title: The K-Book: An Introduction to Algebraic K-Theory
books.author: Charles A. Weibel
books.version: 2013 author edition
books.note: A long introduction spanning low-dimensional groups and higher algebraic K-theory.
books.use: Main course text and reference for K-theory.

books.title: Complex Cobordism and Stable Homotopy Groups of Spheres
books.author: Douglas C. Ravenel
books.version: Author-hosted edition; original book 1986
books.note: Studies complex cobordism and computational tools in stable homotopy.

books.title: Geometry and Higher Category Theory
books.author: Peter Scholze
books.version: Winter semester 2025–26
books.note: A recent course relating geometric ideas and higher categorical structures.
books.use: Advanced seminar reading rather than an undergraduate introduction.

books.title: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
books.author: The Univalent Foundations Program
books.version: 2013; official updated PDF options
books.note: Develops univalent foundations through dependent type theory and homotopical ideas.
books.prerequisites: Mathematical logic; some category theory or topology.
books.use: Learn a foundation connected to formal proof systems.

books.title: Basic Category Theory
books.author: Tom Leinster
books.version: Book 2014; arXiv revised 2025
books.note: A short introduction to categorical structures, universal properties and adjunctions.

books.title: Higher Operads, Higher Categories
books.author: Tom Leinster
books.version: 2004; author arXiv edition
books.note: Uses generalized operads to organize several higher-categorical structures.

books.title: Lectures on the Theorem of Browder and Novikov and Siebenmann’s Thesis
books.author: Michel A. Kervaire
books.version: TIFR volume 46; retypeset digital edition (see PDF imprint for publication year)
books.note: Studies surgery-theoretic and topological manifold results. Historical notation may differ from current treatments. Individual-use access only; do not redistribute.
